title: Number of Day Activity Centres for Special Needs Persons
what_it_is: Number of Day Activity Centres for Special Needs Persons

sections.label: Clients and young adults
sections.summary: As of August 2018, there are about 1,200 clients, of whom about 200, or 17%, are young adults aged 18 to 21.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: As of August 2018, there are about 1,200 clients, of whom about 200 or 17% are young adults between the ages of 18 and 21.

sections.label: DAC staff and training officers
sections.summary: DAC training officers, the direct care workers, support clients and assist professionals, with about 70 professionals and 250 direct care workers across 30 DACs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The direct care workers, who are known as DAC training officers, support the clients and assist the professionals in their day-to-day activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There are a total of about 70 professionals and 250 direct care workers across the 30 DACs.

sections.label: Employment training under Enabling Masterplan 3
sections.summary: Under the Enabling Masterplan 3, MSF has been discussing and working with MOE and SkillsFuture Singapore to identify suitable employment-related training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Under the Enabling Masterplan 3, MSF has been discussing and working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) and SkillsFuture Singapore to identify suitable employment-related training.

sections.label: Post-SPED options at age 18
sections.summary: MSF has been working with MOE and SPED schools to identify upstream orientation programmes for students who finish SPED education at age 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: When they finish their SPED education at age 18, where do they go?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We have been working with MOE and SPED schools to identify upstream orientation programmes.

sections.label: DAC costs and task force proposal
sections.summary: A volunteer running a DAC notes high running costs and asks if MSF would consider a task force on adults beyond 18 and 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From my other life, which is running a DAC as a volunteer, I know that the cost of running DACs is very high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It can go up to almost half a million dollars of deficit each year for less than 50 people who have moderate to severe disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I think the need will go beyond 21 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I was wondering if MSF would consider assembling a small task force to look at the challenges facing this group of adults beyond 18, 21, and look at how to configure solutions that will involve not only the people sector, but also the public and private sectors, and other donors and foundations that can come together.

sections.label: MSF open to task force
sections.summary: MSF says it is open to discussing working with the community, donors and DACs, and would invite the Member to serve on a task force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The answer to the Member's question is yes, we are open to discussing how we can work together with the community, the donors, the DACs to make sure that we will be able to provide adequate and affordable services to their clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So, when we do, indeed, form a task force, I would be happy to invite the Member to serve on the task force so that we can work together and the Member can provide her perspective and insights on how we can work together collectively to make Singapore a more inclusive society for all, including those with disabilities.
